daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Attorney General's Office defended the guilty verdict against former Education Minister Nadiem Makarim despite one judge issuing a dissenting opinion, with the Kejagung emphasizing that other judges found him guilty. The controversy deepened as questions arose about the whereabouts of fugitive Jurist Tan following the verdict. The Kejagung also clarified that Supreme Court permission does not apply when conducting hand-catching operations against judges in corruption cases.

  • The government and DPR agreed on macro assumptions for the 2027 state budget draft, with Indonesia eyeing higher regional welfare in the 2027 budget plan.
  • The process surrounding a right of inquiry by the Gowa regional parliament was reported to Bareskrim for allegedly exposing private matters.
  • Labor groups declared a large coalition with prominent union leader Said Iqbal absent, as he stated he already has his own coalition.
  • A Commission V leader reminded ride-hailing app operators not to pass the 8 percent commission burden onto consumers.
  • Ombudsman official Hery Susanto denied intimidating subordinates during the preparation of an Ombudsman investigation report.
  • The lawyer representing former President Jokowi in a diploma lawsuit refused to show the diploma as mediation reached a deadlock.
  • The PANRB Minister stated that bureaucratic transformation must provide legal certainty.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Belarus launched a 2026-2030 cooperation roadmap, with the Belarusian president viewing Indonesia as a key Southeast Asia partner. The two countries signed collaboration agreements in medical education and pharmaceuticals, while Belarus offered technology transfer to support Indonesia's food security.

  • Indonesia and Australia encouraged stronger cooperation in food and infrastructure sectors.
  • Indonesia strengthened Natuna defense against transnational crimes.

Other

Finance Minister Purbaya rejected the proposal to make the new capital IKN an international financial center, citing the location as too isolated, even as the government separately plans facilities for its international financial center. The Ministry of Finance will appoint more marketplace companies as tax collectors. Indonesia's foreign trade remains strong despite a May deficit, according to the Trade Minister.

  • The KPK is investigating a suspected extortion scheme by several immigration offices targeting foreign nationals to avoid deportation, and detained one more private sector suspect in a bribery case involving a BPK audit of the Muara Enim regent, while interrogating the wife and child of former MPR Secretary General Ma'ruf Cahyono about assets in a gratification case.
  • A police brigadier general serving as secretary to a BGN deputy became a suspect in MBG corruption, while the KPK reportedly conducted a hand-catching operation in North Sumatra.
  • The Social Affairs Minister revealed that 833 PKH assistants were found to hold dual jobs and must return their salaries.
  • BPJS Kesehatan reported that service expenditures in 2025 reached Rp 191.33 trillion with a claim ratio above 100 percent.
  • The government is preparing a pension scheme for athletes after retirement, with the Youth and Sports Minister issuing an ultimatum not to corrupt the fund.
  • Indonesia reviews Apple services under new child protection rules, while the Communications Ministry reported that many elderly fell victim to AI scams mimicking officials' voices.
